clusters.title: [Impact] KB5122871 on Config2 - Schannel TLS path has no defense in depth
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:schannel-tls:Config2 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Schannel Remote Code Execution Vulnerability | [KB5122871](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-72940) | CVE-2026-72940 | Install - High Prio |
| Windows Schannel Denial of Service Vulnerability | [KB5122871](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-70575) | CVE-2026-70575 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: Config2
- Model / role: LabBench-L110 / lab-analysis-workstation
- Deployment group: lab-ring-0
- OS: Windows 11 IoT Enterprise build 10.0.26100.4200
- Clinical criticality: high
- Network exposure: restricted_lan

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | C | H | H |
| Product | M | M | M |

Letters are C / H / M / L. Vendor comes from FindUpdates severity, KEV, and exploitability. Product is allowed to be lower when the patched component is not loaded.

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

- `src/HostApplication/HostApplication.csproj` — `UseWPF`, WinExe, `net9.0-windows`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `dotnet publish` `--self-contained true` `-r win-x64`.
- `src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs` — `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt`.
- `src/HostApplication.Core/SystemInformation.cs` — `RuntimeInformation` host strings.
- `src/HostApplication/app.manifest` — Windows 10 compatibility and `PerMonitorV2`.
- `src/HostApplication.Core/InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs` — HTTPS via host Schannel.
- SBOM present at `workspace/sbom/HostApplication.sbom.spdx.json`.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The published exe still starts without this KB. `HostApplication.csproj` has no third-party `PackageReference` for the patched library, and CI publishes `--self-contained true`. This host KB is not a product runtime patch.
- **If we install: Compatible with the app.** Putting the KB on the host does not replace bits inside the self-contained exe. The bulletin HTTPS client still calls host Schannel the same way.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Leaving the KB off leaves that host TLS stack unpatched. `InsecureVendorBulletinClient` uses host Schannel, so the station path stays exposed even though the app keeps running.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Current `main` already runs against today's host Schannel; we did not find an API/ABI break in `InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs`.

### Conclusions

Schannel TLS path has no defense in depth. Current `main` has no third-party PackageReference. CI publishes a self-contained win-x64 exe, so an OS .NET KB does not patch the bundled runtime.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-72940, CVE-2026-70575 in KB5122871. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed that the vendor bulletin HTTPS client uses host Schannel. The process has that host dependency.

## Product Risk assessment

- Affected product functions: vendor bulletin HTTPS check (`CheckBulletinCommand`).
- Potential hazards: untrusted TLS if the host Schannel stack stays exposed and the client accepts a bad chain.
- Failure scenarios: skip — host TLS remains unpatched; install — handshake behavior may change, bulletin fetch may fail closed.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `TC-UNIT-TLS-MARKER`
- `TC-REG-TLS-CALLBACK`

### Gap Analysis

- No UI automation for the bulletin button.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio: lab-check the published win-x64 build for Config2 against this `schannel-tls` coupling. Do not instruct production install from this analysis.
